text: This is Attune. Pages that negotiate with your agent, instead of tracking you.

caption: Two bad options: be tracked, or be summarized.
text: When you read with an AI beside you, you get two bad options. Let the site track you into a personalized experience. Or let the AI scrape the page and summarize it, losing the figures, the interactives, the author's voice, and sometimes the facts. WebMCP makes a third way possible: the page can simply ask your agent what you need.

caption: Your agent declares five facets. The page composes an edition from the author's own blocks.
text: Here is an article about WebMCP. I tell my agent: I have three minutes, I already know MCP, give me the expert version. The agent calls one tool, declare reader context. The page recomposes itself: a three-minute expert edition, built only from blocks the author wrote, skipping what I already know. The Handshake panel shows exactly what my agent said, and I can change or erase it.

caption: Level, language, time, goal, known concepts — every decision has a visible reason.
text: Now I want the full beginner version, in Korean. One more call. Nothing is generated: every sentence in every edition was written by the author, in both languages. Trimming, ordering and prerequisites are decided by a deterministic composer, and the outline tells you why each block is in or out.

caption: The page notices where you got stuck. Your agent swaps in the author's plainer version.
text: Now the part I love. The page notices, locally, when I re-read a paragraph. My agent can ask where I got stuck, and swap in the author's plainer version of that exact block, right where I am. No rewriting, no hallucination, just the author's own simpler words.

caption: Interactives become tools: your agent operates the calculator on the page.
text: Interactives stop being pictures. In the compound interest article, I ask: what if I put in five hundred a month for forty years with a one percent fee? The agent sets the calculator's parameters through a tool, the chart on the page changes, and the agent gets the exact numbers I am looking at.

caption: Ask the author: answers in the author's own words, or “not covered”.
text: Questions go to the author, not to a guess. Ask author returns the writer's own answers, and says plainly when something was not covered. Then I say forget me, and the page erases everything it knew.

caption: For publishers: anonymous demand signals. No identifiers, ever.
text: For the publisher, the only thing the server ever stores is a count of which edition shapes readers asked for. What readers asked for, without knowing who they are. That is a new deal between readers, authors and agents, and it runs on nothing but WebMCP and a little structure in the content.

caption: Tool surfaces follow the page. Every result carries a next step.
text: Under the hood: two tool surfaces swapped with abort signals, seventeen tools on an article, read-only hints on reads, loose schemas with strict validation, and a next step in every result. A deterministic composer with unit tests, three original articles at three levels in two languages, and an end-to-end suite that drives every tool like an agent.
Attune. Bring your agent. The page will meet you where you are. Attune dot znehraks dot workers dot dev.
